homonyms.basis: No card is a homonym, and T composes the dataset itself (per_dim reached 'same'). Wikipedia's article carries a hatnote to 'Pile (disambiguation)'; no other sense of the name is on the rail or in T. 'The Pile' and 'Pile' are the census's other names for the entity. The distinct entities below are named by the field, the census or the archive beside the entity and are never senses of its name.
distinct_entities: the Common Pile v0.1, its successor (June 2025), a distinct dataset (F23, F68; TLL-30)
Common Crawl, the source of its Pile-CC component and a row of its own in the census (F13, F44; TLL-33)
Books3, a component, and The Atlantic's search tool over it, a census row of its own (books3-search) (F15, F41)
Bibliotik, the private tracker Books3 was copied from (F15, F41)
Project Gutenberg and PG-19, the source of a component, a census row of its own (F42)
Data Portraits, a paper and tool that documents it, a census row of its own (F77, F78)
the Rights Alliance, which took Books3 down (F16)
Hugging Face, host of its dataset card and of the Common Pile announcement (F33, F68)

captures.description: THE DATASET, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'The Pile is an 825 GiB to 886 GB open-source English text dataset created by EleutherAI and released on December 31, 2020, to train large language models (LLMs).' Key overview (size, '~825 GiB compressed (zstandard format) containing roughly 300 billion tokens'; composition; purpose; 'Notable Models Trained On It: GPT-Neo, GPT-J, and the Pythia suite by EleutherAI'); the 22 sub-datasets, numbered, 'Books3 (Long-form literary text/books)' third and 'Gutenberg (PG-19) (Public domain literature)' eleventh; controversies and evolution ('resulting in content adjustments'; Common Pile v0.1). Eight cards: the Pile's home page, Wikipedia, Hugging Face, Reddit r/MachineLearning, the Pile's paper page, a YouTube paper reading, Hugging Face on the Common Pile v0.1, Michael Brenndoerfer.

atoms.evidence: The Pile is an 825 GiB to 886 GB open-source English text dataset created by EleutherAI
created by EleutherAI and released on December 31, 2020
open-source English text dataset created by EleutherAI and released on December 31, 2020, to train large language models (LLMs).
Combines 22 diverse sub-datasets across academic, web, prose, and code domains.
Designed to improve cross-domain knowledge, reasoning, and generalization compared to raw web scrapes like Common Crawl.
